paras: Anaya was walking home from school with her friends Arjun and Krishna. Near the park, she saw a brown wallet lying on the road. She picked it up. Inside there was some money and a card with a name and a phone number on it.

“Wow, so much money! Let’s buy ice creams,” said Krishna. Anaya shook her head. “This is not ours. Somebody must be looking for it.” She took the wallet to her father, and he called the number on the card. The owner came and thanked Anaya with a big smile.
That evening, the lights suddenly went off. It was a power cut! The whole house became dark. Arjun was scared and started to cry. Krishna ran towards the door and bumped into a chair.

“Stop! Stay where you are,” said Anaya calmly. “If we run in the dark, we may get hurt.” She remembered where the torch was kept. She walked slowly, found it and switched it on. Soon everyone felt safe again.
On Saturday, Anaya went to the shop with her pocket money of ₹50. She wanted a toy car that cost ₹40. Then she saw a story book that cost ₹30. She could not buy both.

Anaya thought for a while. “I already have many toys, but I have no new book to read,” she said. She bought the story book. She kept the remaining ₹20 in her piggy bank and decided to save for the toy car.

When Anaya reached home, her grandmother had a surprise. She had brought 5 sweet mangoes for Anaya, Arjun and Krishna. “How shall we share them?” asked Arjun. “I want two!” said Krishna. “That is not fair,” said Anaya.

Grandmother smiled. “Let each friend take one mango first. Then we will cut the last two mangoes into three equal pieces each. Every friend will get two pieces more.” Everyone got the same share, and nobody was upset. They enjoyed the mangoes together.

items.q: What did Anaya do when she found the wallet? Why did she do that?
items.a: She gave it to her father so that it could be returned. The wallet did not belong to her, and the owner must have been looking for it.

items.q: Why did Anaya say, “Stop! Stay where you are,” during the power cut?
items.a: Because if they ran in the dark, they might bump into things and get hurt.

items.q: Anaya could not buy both the toy car and the story book. What did she choose, and why?
items.a: She chose the story book because she already had many toys but no new book to read. She saved the rest of her money for the toy car.

items.q: Why was it not fair when Krishna said, “I want two mangoes!”?
items.a: Because there were three friends, and everyone should get the same share.

sections.heading: B. Match the situation with the sensible thing to do.

items.l: You find a wallet on the road.
items.r: Give it to a grown-up so that it reaches its owner.

items.l: The lights go off at night.
items.r: Stay calm and use a torch.

items.l: You want two things but have money for only one.
items.r: Choose the one you need more.

items.l: Three friends have to share mangoes.
items.r: Divide them equally so that everyone gets the same.
